title: BCCI Maps Long-Term Career Plan for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Drawing Sachin Tendulkar Parallels
excerpt: Board secretary Devajit Saikia says the 15-year-old prodigy is being closely monitored to ensure sustained success, with VVS Laxman overseeing his development through the Centre of Excellence.
body:
• BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia says the board is taking a long-term view of Sooryavanshi's career, drawing explicit parallels to Sachin Tendulkar's longevity
  • Sooryavanshi's development featured prominently at a high-level BCCI review meeting in Mumbai attended by captain Shubman Gill, head coach Gautam Gambhir, and CoE head VVS Laxman
  • The 15-year-old has scored 776 IPL runs at a strike rate of 237.30, 151 runs against Zimbabwe, and become the youngest Duleep Trophy half-centurion
  • BCCI has identified 10-15 young prospects in a targeted development group monitored by Laxman's Centre of Excellence

The Board of Control for Cricket in India is building a long-term development plan around 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, with secretary Devajit Saikia making a direct comparison to Sachin Tendulkar's career trajectory and pledging that the board will protect the teenager from burnout or premature pressure.

Sooryavanshi's future was a central topic at Thursday's high-level BCCI review meeting in Mumbai, attended by India Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill, T20I captain Shreyas Iyer, head coach Gautam Gambhir, and Centre of Excellence head VVS Laxman.

"We want Vaibhav Sooryavanshi or any player of his stature to continue and serve like Sachin Tendulkar did for the country or other players who in the past became legends."

— Devajit Saikia, BCCI Secretary

Not a One-Series Wonder

Saikia stressed that the BCCI's priority is sustainable development over immediate returns. The board wants Sooryavanshi to build a career that spans years, not a burst of fireworks that fades quickly.

"We are very cautious that every right step he should take forward so that it should not be a one series or one year wonder," Saikia said. "He's monitored from every angle and every step he is taking forward in his international career."

The Tendulkar comparison is deliberate and carries weight. Tendulkar debuted for India at 16 in 1989 and went on to amass 34,357 international runs across 24 years — the gold standard for turning teenage promise into generational greatness. The BCCI is using that blueprint as a reference point for managing Sooryavanshi's workload and exposure.

From IPL Sensation to International Stage

Sooryavanshi's rise has been relentless. His IPL 2026 campaign with Rajasthan Royals produced 776 runs in 16 matches at a strike rate of 237.30, with a century, five half-centuries, and a record 72 sixes in a single season. He swept the awards — Orange Cap, Most Valuable Player, Emerging Player, Super Striker, and Super Sixes.

India's youngest-ever men's international debutant then scored 151 runs in three T20Is against Zimbabwe as India completed a 3-0 sweep, earning his maiden Player of the Series award. His opening series against England was tougher, but the Zimbabwe rebound confirmed a player who can learn and adjust fast.

Duleep Trophy Milestone

Sooryavanshi has continued to push boundaries in domestic cricket. At 15 years and 157 days, he became the youngest batter to score a half-century in Duleep Trophy history, breaking a record that had stood for 57 years. He struck 92 off 81 deliveries in the semi-final against Central Zone for East Zone, then added 40 in the second innings.

His availability for the Duleep Trophy final — East Zone vs. South Zone at Chennai's MA Chidambaram Stadium from September 6 — will depend on head coach Gambhir's decision, according to Saikia.

Broader Talent Pipeline

The BCCI's developmental focus extends beyond one player. Saikia revealed that 10-15 promising cricketers have been placed in a targeted monitoring group, with VVS Laxman directly overseeing their training and skill progression through the Centre of Excellence.

"There are about 10-15 players who are in our targeted group. They are constantly monitored by our COE head, VVS Laxman, who is taking keen interest in their future and their training and skill development."

— Devajit Saikia, BCCI Secretary

The infrastructure gives Sooryavanshi and other young players a structured pathway from age-group cricket to the international stage — a shift from the ad hoc talent development that previous generations navigated largely on their own.

What's Next

Sooryavanshi is part of India's T20I squad for the three-match series against Afghanistan beginning September 13. He is also set to travel with India's Asian Games squad to Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, where the cricket competition starts September 24 under Laxman's coaching.

The BCCI's message is clear: Sooryavanshi has the talent. The board's job now is to ensure it lasts.
